name: West Coast Swing
notes: West Coast Swing style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). Lineage told straight and tied to this app's own Lindy pack: WCS descends from Lindy Hop — a Black American dance born in Harlem — carried to Los Angeles by the Dean Collins generation of Savoy-style dancers in the 1940s-50s, where it evolved into a slotted, smooth, elastic dance fused with R&B and blues. It is California's official state dance. Today it's danced to pop, R&B and blues at 80-100 BPM, and its scene prizes improvisation and conversation between partners over patterns. Solo-first design: the slot (a straight lane), walk-walk triple-triple rhythm, the anchor step (WCS's signature 'come home' moment), rolling-through-the-feet smoothness, and elastic-connection prep all train alone; partnered basics (sugar push, passes, whips) are flagged 🤝 and live at classes and socials — the WCS scene runs beginner lessons before nearly every dance.

seasons.finale: Tell it on camera: Harlem to the Savoy to Dean Collins' LA — then film the walk-walk triple-triple down your slot.
Film the 6-count rhythm traveling a straight slot, both directions — smooth, rolling, on the walking beat.
Film ten clean anchor steps — settled back, connected to an imaginary partner, never creeping forward.
Film the stretch-and-release drill: slot rhythm with a resistance band or doorframe, elasticity visible.
Find the WCS night near you — take the beginner lesson (there's always one), stay for the social.

attributes.name: Rolling walk L1
attributes.test: 20 slow walks rolling heel-to-toe with a level head — WCS smoothness is a walking skill

attributes.name: Half-time ear L1
attributes.test: clap 2 and 4 (the backbeat) through one full 90-BPM pop or blues track without drifting

attributes.name: Anchor core L1
attributes.test: 10 controlled sit-back holds (weight settled back over the rear foot, 3s each) without tipping

nodes.name: Slow grooves — the 80-100 BPM pocket
checkpoints: WCS lives slow: pop, R&B and blues around 80-100 BPM — room to say something in every count
the backbeat (2 and 4) is your anchor; the bass line is your conversation partner
one dance, any radio station — WCS is the swing that followed the music forward

nodes.name: Musicality — dancing the song, not the pattern
checkpoints: WCS judges and dancers prize hitting the song: breaks, builds, lyrics
patterns are sentences you can pause, stretch, or interrupt when the music asks
listen to one WCS-night playlist per week; the scene's musicality starts in the ears

nodes.name: From the Savoy to the slot
checkpoints: West Coast Swing descends from Lindy Hop — a Black American dance born in Harlem's ballrooms
Savoy-style dancers of the Dean Collins generation carried it to Los Angeles in the 1940s-50s, where crowded floors and film work smoothed it into a slotted dance
it fused with R&B and blues, kept evolving with every decade's music, and became California's official state dance
same root as this app's Lindy pack — two branches of one Harlem tree

nodes.name: The modern scene — conversation over choreography
checkpoints: WCS is lead-follow improvisation — the follow's voice is half the dance, and the scene treats it that way
weekly dances run a beginner lesson first, almost everywhere on earth
conventions and Jack & Jills (random-partner contests) are the scene's heartbeat — watch one final online and count how much is invented on the spot

nodes.name: The slot & the 6-count rhythm
nodes.anchor: WCS's home shape — a straight lane you own
checkpoints: walk-walk, triple-step, triple-step — six counts traveling a straight line
the slot is a lane, not a wander: pick two floor points and dance between them
walks are real walks — rolling, grounded, unhurried
both directions, both starting feet
mistakes: bouncing the triples — WCS stays smooth and low
curving the slot into a circle

nodes.name: The anchor step
nodes.anchor: the signature of the whole dance
checkpoints: the final triple of every pattern, danced IN PLACE with weight settled back — never traveling forward
the anchor is where connection re-gathers: sit into it like the end of a sentence
count '5-and-6', settle on 5, stay home through 6
creeping forward on the anchor is WCS's cardinal sin — film yourself and check
mistakes: drifting toward your (imaginary) partner during the anchor
rushing off the anchor before the next pattern asks

nodes.name: Rolling through the feet
checkpoints: every step peels through the foot — WCS's smoothness is articulation, not stiffness
half-time drills: the slot rhythm at 50% speed, every roll visible
level head, soft knees, zero bounce — the glide test

nodes.name: Elastic connection prep (solo)
checkpoints: WCS connection stretches and releases like a rubber band — never a yank, never slack
band or doorframe drill: walk the slot away until the stretch builds, ride it back in
the anchor is where the stretch lives — settle back, feel the band load, release into the walks

nodes.name: Sugar push & passes (with a partner)
checkpoints: sugar push, left-side pass, right-side pass — the first three sentences of the conversation, learned at the beginner lesson
the whip comes later; the anchor you already own is what makes all of them work
rotate partners at the lesson — fifty conversations beat one rehearsal

nodes.name: One song down the slot — filmed
checkpoints: one slow song: slot rhythm, anchors settled, one musical hit on a break
watch it back for the anchors first — did any creep?
smoothness check: could a glass of water ride your head?

nodes.name: The WCS night
checkpoints: find the weekly WCS dance near you — beginner lesson first, social after, everywhere
dance with strangers; the scene was built for it
afterward, watch a Jack & Jill final and spot the anchors you now understand
